screens.name: Home — default, transition and large text
screens.evidence: Sheets 29–31 show a seated painted orb and readable omen status, while supplied runtime evidence reports complete-hero and contrast checks.
findings: Strengthen the omen card’s lower boundary so its cropped edge above navigation looks like scrollable content rather than an unfinished panel.

screens.name: Home — successful omen fixture and expanded unavailable-omen policy
screens.evidence: Sheet 30 distinguishes a sample omen from an unavailable daily attempt and shows the enlarged expanded policy filling most of the viewport.
findings: Shorten and group the centered failure policy so the explanation does not visually outweigh the main reading action.

screens.name: Home — room destinations and omen loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 47 shows Shelf, Hearth and Cabinet as small painted thumbnails, with supplied runtime evidence reporting 44×44 targets and correct routes.
findings: Integrate the destination thumbnails with consistent frames, contact shadows and lighting so they feel like objects in the room.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheet 33 presents two explicit age answers at both scales, and the supplied age checks report persistent restriction and keyboard focus behavior.
findings: Give the secondary age answer a clearer bounded interaction area while preserving its lower emphasis.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheet 34 shows labeled blank date fields reflowing from three columns to two plus a full-width year at large text.
findings: Provide visible field-format guidance and demonstrate readable entered dates on the parchment inputs.

screens.name: Age blocked — onboarding and saved-birthday restriction
screens.evidence: Sheets 1 and 34–35 show an explicit age restriction and correction route, supported by supplied no-bypass and correction checks.
findings: Render the sole correction action with a stronger button affordance so recovery is immediately apparent.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheets 35–36 show the correction explanation, date fields and Check birthday action, with the large-text action at the viewport bottom.
findings: Reduce the stacked introductory height and establish a visible populated-date example without shrinking enlarged text.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected and optional skip
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 36–37 show four parchment choices and an explicit skip route, with enlarged choices pushing completion below the initial viewport.
findings: Replace the unexplained instruction to choose a charm with concise wording that names the visible focus choices.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 36–37 show a check beside Learning & growth and a changed Save focus and continue action.
findings: Add a subtle selected border or fill change so the check is not the only spatially small selection cue.

screens.name: Birthday editing — default
screens.evidence: Sheet 56 shows an existing-profile birthday editor with visually blank fields, Save, Cancel and a collapsed removal action.
findings: Show the existing birthday visibly in the editor so users can inspect what Save will retain or replace.

screens.name: Birthday editing — invalid and partial
screens.evidence: Sheets 1–2 show specific date errors but no visible attempted values, despite supplied runtime claims that invalid and partial drafts are retained.
findings: Make the retained attempted date visible alongside the error so users can identify and correct the offending entry.

screens.name: Birth time — initial and profile entry
screens.evidence: Sheets 8–9 and 55 show a labeled time field, 24-hour explanation and an explicit unknown-time alternative.
findings: Place a visible HH:MM example inside or immediately beside the field and demonstrate readable entered time.

screens.name: Birth time — invalid
screens.evidence: Sheet 9 shows focused time input and a precise 00:00–23:59 error, but the rejected value is not visible.
findings: Keep the invalid time visibly readable while showing the allowed range and focused field.

screens.name: Birth details — forgotten
screens.evidence: Sheet 8 explicitly confirms that time and place were forgotten while birthday remains, at both text scales.
findings: Separate the completion confirmation from the new-entry form with a compact centered status group.

screens.name: Birth city — empty and retained draft
screens.evidence: Sheets 6–7 and 54–55 show visually blank city fields in both empty and draft-retained captures while the search action changes availability.
findings: Restore visible city draft text so the enabled search action has an inspectable query.

screens.name: Birth city — service failure and retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 7 shows explicit search unavailability, Retry city search and preservation copy, but no visible retained query.
findings: Display the retained city query above the retry action so recovery clearly repeats the intended search.

screens.name: Birth city — no results
screens.evidence: Sheets 7–8 give spelling and nearby-town recovery advice, while the query field remains visually blank.
findings: Show the failed query and shorten the centered no-results message to keep correction close to the input.

screens.name: Birth city — live results
screens.evidence: Sheets 9–10 show disambiguated Copenhagen results, with large decorative labels taking several lines and no visible search query.
findings: Use centered city titles with smaller region/country lines and restore the visible query above the results.

screens.name: Birth profile — saved and successful retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show the calculated Moon/rising result, saved-on-device confirmation, location/time and edit/forget routes.
findings: Group the chart result and supporting birth details more tightly to reduce the tall enlarged result block.

screens.name: Ask approach — normal, transition and large
screens.evidence: Sheet 3 shows a painted orb seated above the question prompt and distinct type/voice routes, with a sharper room in the transition capture.
findings: Keep room focus and table lighting more consistent through the approach transition so the orb remains anchored to one scene.

screens.name: Ask — collapsed self and named-person question
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–6 show the subject, collapsed disclosure, focused paper editor and primary submit at normal and large text.
findings: Demonstrate readable populated question text and an explicit empty-submit state rather than relying on the blank-paper captures.

screens.name: Ask — expanded context disclosure
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 show the data disclosure occupying nearly the entire large-text viewport before the question field begins.
findings: Condense the centered disclosure into short labeled groups so inspecting shared details does not bury question entry.

screens.name: Named-person input — default, empty and valid
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6 and 27 show Someone selected, but the valid-name capture has no visible name despite supplied runtime confirmation of valid-name entry.
findings: Make entered names visibly readable and keep the confirmation state inspectable in the constrained viewport.

screens.name: Questionnaire — cards 1, 2 and 3 unselected
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–13 show consistent progress, radio choices, own-words alternatives and dimmed continuation controls at both scales.
findings: Give disabled continuation a slightly clearer boundary while retaining the visible choose-first instruction.

screens.name: Questionnaire — selected answer
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows a filled Time radio and brightened Continue, supported by supplied keyboard-selection and back-restoration checks.
findings: Add a restrained selected-row treatment to reinforce the small radio indicator across text scales.

screens.name: Questionnaire — own-words empty answer
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 show a focused empty answer field, expand action and explicit write-to-continue instruction.
findings: Bring the write-to-continue instruction closer to the field so its relationship remains clear at large text.

screens.name: Questionnaire — populated custom answer and constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheets 25–26 show an enabled Reveal and long-answer scroll cue while the supposedly populated answer paper appears entirely blank.
findings: Restore visible answer text before allowing a user to submit content they cannot inspect.

screens.name: Expanded editors — question and custom answer at both scales
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show blank paper with nonzero 300/300 and 489/500 character counters in both enlarged and normal editors.
findings: Fix the missing visible draft rendering and recapture populated editors with readable text, selection and caret.

screens.name: Ask — constrained typing, long question and retrieved disclosure
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–27 show reachable question actions and scroll cues in constrained captures but no visible text in long-question inputs.
findings: Ensure the entire retained question can be visually read and edited within the constrained viewport.

screens.name: Planning and research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 42–44 show stage-specific loading copy, a stated wait bound and cancellation, with supplied reduced-motion checks.
findings: Give the isolated loading orb a clearer ground shadow or scene support to preserve the physical-room treatment.

screens.name: Plan and prediction errors
screens.evidence: Sheets 20–21 distinguish retry, edit and review-answer recovery and explicitly state that nothing was charged.
findings: Reduce the large empty lower region with a tighter vertically balanced recovery group while retaining centered text.

screens.name: Sensitive plan and prediction redirect
screens.evidence: Sheets 48–49 show a named external support destination, alternative question routes and explicit no-spend/no-memory feedback.
findings: Place the brief reason immediately before the support action so the action has context before users encounter it.

screens.name: Voice unavailable
screens.evidence: Sheets 32–33 show an explicit voice-start failure with typing as the primary fallback and a separate retry.
findings: Distinguish a permission problem from a generic start failure when the browser can establish the cause.

screens.name: Opening — normal and golden charge, release and settle
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–40 show orb and fracture stages before the forecast, while supplied runtime evidence reports seven interruption, skip and reduced-motion paths.
findings: Blend the thin fracture lines into the painted illumination and preserve a consistent grounded shadow through the reveal.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — collapsed and expanded actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 44–47 show the forecast, uncertainty label, check-in date and several similarly styled text actions, with enlarged scrolled content meeting the fixed header.
findings: Separate the forecast from the action group more decisively and keep scrolled text clear of the fixed header.

screens.name: Check-in — no selection
screens.evidence: Sheets 15–17 show three outcomes and a choose-then-save instruction, but each radio is widely separated from its centered label.
findings: Give each outcome a coherent full-width row surface so the radio and label read as one control.

screens.name: Check-in — unsaved selection
screens.evidence: Sheet 17 explicitly distinguishes Not saved yet from the selected Not yet outcome and enables Save outcome.
findings: Keep the save action and unsaved status together when enlarged so the required commit remains obvious.

screens.name: Check-in — saved yes, not quite and not yet
screens.evidence: Sheets 16 and 40 show each selected saved outcome, a Saved button state and instructions for changing the answer.
findings: Use one compact saved-status group to reduce repetition between the confirmation, disabled button and change instruction.

screens.name: Check-in — expanded original question
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows the original question below saved feedback, with large scrolled text visibly cut at the fixed top region.
findings: Add clearer separation and header occlusion so expanded question text does not appear sliced beneath the top controls.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–29 show a centered bottle, first-glimpse prompt and Ask the Ball route in a distinct painted room.
findings: Make Ask the Ball visually more actionable than neighboring explanatory text.

screens.name: History — populated, stress and persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheets 27–29 show parchment readings resting on shelves, with dates, suggested check-ins and a persisted Yes outcome.
findings: Replace the orphaned leading status dots with a clean centered status line and clarify that the whole reading card opens.

screens.name: Sky — selected sample question and offline fallback
screens.evidence: Sheet 53 shows a labeled offline sample, selectable themes and a selected question, while the moon-window surface changes from organic framing to a rectangle at large text.
findings: Preserve one moon-window material and framing treatment across scales and keep the selected question visibly connected to its theme.

screens.name: Circles — offline and failed retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 18–19 distinguish initial offline status from a failed retry and retain a privacy explanation, whose enlarged card continues below navigation.
findings: Make the continuation below the fixed navigation more apparent and keep the privacy card’s physical edge intact.

screens.name: Reading details — disclosures collapsed
screens.evidence: Sheet 45 shows four consistently labeled sections with counts, summaries and disclosure chevrons at both scales.
findings: Give disclosure rows a subtle shared boundary so their full interactive extent is visually clear.

screens.name: Reading details — answers expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 21–22 show lengthy centered answer paragraphs under smaller question labels at normal and enlarged text.
findings: Break long centered answers into shorter readable groups and strengthen spacing between each question-answer pair.

screens.name: Reading details — assumptions expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 22–23 show a counted assumption section, long centered content and a dedicated Close assumptions action.
findings: Use shorter centered paragraph groups and keep the collapse action adjacent to the final content line.

screens.name: Reading details — reason expanded and free Why view
screens.evidence: Sheets 23 and 46–47 show dense centered explanations, saved-explanation context and explicit limits on what background sources establish.
findings: Divide the centered explanation into labeled context, assumption and limitation blocks with shorter paragraphs.

screens.name: Reading details — sources expanded
screens.evidence: Sheet 24 shows a background-only disclaimer, source link, date and long fixture excerpt below the expanded disclosure.
findings: Visually group each source’s title, date and excerpt and use a concise centered excerpt before optional expansion.

screens.name: Plans — weekly and monthly selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 41–42 show explicit test-mode pricing, renewal terms, selected checks and commit actions, supported by supplied keyboard radio checks.
findings: Create a stronger centered price hierarchy and a persistent compact benefit summary so enlarged plan options do not become three equally dense blocks.

screens.name: You — profile, plan and memory
screens.evidence: Sheets 56–57 show a parchment birth profile, free-plan balance and memory controls, with the large profile occupying most of the first viewport.
findings: Reduce redundant spacing within the enlarged birth-profile card so plan and memory remain easier to discover.

screens.name: You — display, sound and data settings
screens.evidence: Sheet 49 shows labeled native-looking switches, an enabled large-text state and separate saved-data actions, with supplied reduced-motion checks.
findings: Give settings groups a restrained consistent surface treatment so modern switches feel connected to the apothecary controls.

screens.name: Share — main and expanded invite/remind options
screens.evidence: Sheets 50–52 show a small preview, Download image, readable image text and privacy scope, with expanded options continuing below the viewport.
findings: Group export, preview inspection and invitation actions separately and prevent the scrolled title from appearing sliced beneath the header.

screens.name: Share — full image inspection and story
screens.evidence: Sheets 50 and 53–54 show a coherent portrait export with a readable-image-text route and explicit speculative labeling.
findings: Increase separation behind the exported forecast lettering so the detailed cabinet painting competes less with the message.

screens.name: Share — image text
screens.evidence: Sheets 51–52 show the forecast, uncertainty, brand and date as separate readable text above Download image.
findings: Use the same human-readable date presentation as the in-app forecast to improve continuity.

screens.name: Invitation — copied link result
screens.evidence: Sheet 32 shows Link copied, share-again and view-link actions, with the enlarged view-link row partly meeting the fixed Done region.
findings: Reserve a clearer safe area above Done so the final disclosure control remains fully visible.

screens.name: Invitation — clipboard fallback
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–20 show explicit copy failure and a wrapped encoded URL directly over the busy cabinet background.
findings: Place the selectable fallback URL on a quiet centered writing surface with clear selection affordance and controlled wrapping.

screens.name: Invitation — sharing canceled
screens.evidence: Sheet 31 explicitly reports sharing closed without confirmation and offers Try again and Done at both scales.
findings: Give Try again a clearer button boundary to match its role as the principal recovery action.

screens.name: Reminder — browser unsupported result
screens.evidence: Sheet 43 clearly states that no browser reminder was scheduled and supplies the fixture date and native-app alternative.
findings: Format the check-back date in words and separate it from the platform explanation for faster centered scanning.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home shows painted reflections, a substantial base and convincing table overlap, while supplied runtime evidence reports geometry, skip and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Carry Home’s contact shadow and support plane into isolated reading-orb states to maintain physical continuity.

components.name: Room destination controls
components.evidence: Sheet 47 shows three small scene thumbnails with labels, and supplied measurements report compliant targets and correct destinations.
findings: Unify thumbnail framing, lighting and physical attachment to the room instead of presenting three pasted scene cutouts.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Room screens show five labeled destinations, an elevated central orb and underlined gold selection at both text scales.
findings: Clarify the scroll-content boundary above the raised central orb so underlying cards do not look accidentally obscured.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Home retains a distinctive script wordmark, but enlarged balances read '1 reading' where normal versions say '1 reading left'.
findings: Keep 'left' in the enlarged balance wording so the quantity remains unambiguously available credit.

components.name: Primary wood button
components.evidence: Wood actions consistently distinguish enabled and disabled states, but repeated broad flat planks have limited visible edge thickness.
findings: Add restrained edge thickness and consistent contact shading without increasing texture behind labels.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold centered text represents navigation, retry, disclosure and destructive actions throughout the sheets with few surface distinctions.
findings: Differentiate action roles with consistent spacing, chevrons and bounded focus treatment while keeping text centered.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Sheets 11–14 show legible parchment options with empty/filled radios and supplied keyboard-state verification.
findings: Reinforce selection with a subtle whole-row treatment in addition to the radio.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Question fields appear blank even in long-question captures and in an expanded editor reporting 489/500 characters.
findings: Restore readable entered text above the paper material and verify its contrast, caret and selection in populated captures.

components.name: Large-text input and expanded editor
components.evidence: Sheets 24–27 show large focus outlines and counters but no visible populated draft at 200% or in constrained-height cases.
findings: Fix the blank populated editor before treating enlargement and draft retention as visually verified.

components.name: Birthday input
components.evidence: Date labels and responsive reflow are visible, but existing, invalid and partial date captures do not display inspectable entered values.
findings: Show retained date values clearly and associate the visible error with its specific field.

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Sheet 33 shows two explicit age choices, and supplied runtime evidence describes restriction persistence and correction behavior.
findings: Make both answer areas visually recognizable as controls while preserving the primary/secondary hierarchy.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 36–37 show unselected and checked parchment focus options with distinct skip and save actions.
findings: Strengthen the selected card treatment and use wording that matches the visible focus options.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheets 10–11 and 56–57 show explicit saved chart/profile details, while the large parchment profile consumes most of a viewport.
findings: Tighten internal grouping and give the parchment a more consistent lower edge and contact shadow.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: The form provides specific errors, optional routes and result choices, but retained time and city inputs remain visibly blank.
findings: Make retained input values readable across initial, failure, retry and result states.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Sheet 27’s valid-name state shows a focused blank field despite the supplied successful first-name entry result.
findings: Render the entered name visibly and keep selection, validation and confirmation within an inspectable flow.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheet 49 shows consistent label/switch rows and a visibly enabled large-text switch, with supplied motion-preference checks.
findings: Give the switch group a quiet shared background to reconcile the modern control styling with the room.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 30–31 and 47 show loading, successful fixture, unavailable and expanded-policy states in parchment cards.
findings: Condense the unavailable policy and preserve a clear card boundary above fixed navigation.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 53 uses spatial star labels at normal size and a rectangular text grid at large size with a selected Love question.
findings: Maintain consistent window framing across layouts and make the selected theme/question relationship more explicit.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheets 18–19 show clear offline/retry messaging and a physically edged privacy parchment, but no connected-circle state.
findings: Retain the strong offline explanation and provide connected-circle evidence before grading that unrepresented behavior.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 27–29 show bottles behind parchment readings seated on shelves, including saved outcome and check-in variants.
findings: Simplify the status punctuation and strengthen whole-card interaction affordance.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 41–42 show checked weekly/monthly options and complete renewal terms, with supplied keyboard radio and explicit-commit checks.
findings: Make price, billing interval and renewal detail three distinct centered levels rather than similarly weighted lines.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sheets 50–54 show a cohesive portrait composition, a small main preview and separate full-image and readable-text routes.
findings: Increase the main preview’s inspectability or make its full-image affordance adjacent and unmistakable.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Age, city, voice, reading, sharing and reminder states explicitly describe failure or completion and provide contextual next steps.
findings: Standardize recovery-button treatment where essential retries currently appear as plain gold text.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Sheets 21–24 and 45 show counts, summaries and visible expansion states, but long centered content becomes difficult to scan.
findings: Keep centered text while introducing shorter paragraphs, stronger subsection grouping and consistent disclosure-row boundaries.

components.name: Export and invitation status
components.evidence: Sheets 19–20 and 31–32 show copied, denied-copy and canceled outcomes, while supplied runtime evidence reports PNG generation and mocked sharing.
findings: Put fallback links on a quiet selectable surface and keep status and dismissal controls unobscured at large text.

components.name: Typography and centered spacing
components.evidence: Storybook headings are consistent, but enlarged labels and long centered explanations create tall, repetitive blocks across evidence, plans and birth search.
findings: Retain centered alignment while shortening interface copy, separating supporting lines and breaking explanations into compact paragraphs.

components.name: Atmospheric background and scene layers
components.evidence: The sheets show cabinet, hearth, shelves, foreground bottles and depth blur, while supplied runtime evidence reports desktop performance and reduced-motion passes.
findings: Improve consistent object contact, destination framing and focus continuity rather than adding more texture to the painted room.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser scores; deferred physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native keyboard, voice, haptics and device performance were not used as blanket deductions.
This evaluation uses the supplied screenshots and runtime narrative only; reported automated and live results were not independently rerun.

The character counters prove a populated-editor presentation discrepancy: fields with 300/300 and 489/500 characters appear blank; whether this originates in browser rendering or capture composition is not established.
Essential unreadable draft content triggers the rubric’s overall-at-most-5 gate for the populated editors and affected input components; numeric averages must not conceal that failure.
Static transition and opening frames support composition comparisons but cannot independently establish smooth camera motion, parallax, timing or frame-rate performance.
Reported browser contrast, keyboard, reduced-motion and runtime checks support provisional scoring, but zero axe violations do not resolve the visible blank populated fields.
Synthetic forecast, source, error and future-date fixture wording was treated as fixture evidence rather than a production-copy or model-quality defect.
Connected Circles, successful browser voice capture and actual external share delivery are not demonstrated by the represented states; no functionality was inferred from their controls.
For each item, A is the mean of its applicable first three dimensions and F the mean of its applicable last three; overall uses 0.4A + 0.6F with the stated gates.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across the represented screens and components.
topFixes: Resolve the visibly blank populated inputs first, then capture readable long questions, answers, names, dates and city drafts at normal and 200% text.
Prevent scrolled content from appearing sliced beneath fixed headers and footers, especially check-in, sharing, invitation results and room cards.
Preserve centered typography while shortening interface copy and splitting long explanations into compact labeled groups.
Improve physical integration of room thumbnails, wood-button edges, isolated orbs and the large-text Sky window with consistent lighting and contact shadows.
Strengthen whole-row selected states and secondary-action affordances, then repeat the affected browser state captures and keyboard checks.
